Note: this module requires upgrading OpenSearch to 3.8 from August 2026

OpenSearch Relevance Workbench for Mage-OS

Compare catalog-search results, rate products, and apply a bounded relevance change from Mage-OS Admin. OpenSearch Relevance Workbench provides saved merchant reviews and an advanced evaluation workspace backed by OpenSearch Search Relevance Workbench.

This is an experimental extension. The human workflow includes explicit activation and rollback. Optional LLM judgments are disabled by default and require a separately reviewed runtime. Production support, representative provider calibration, and merchant usability qualification remain open.

The canonical source and issue tracker are in the Mage-OS Lab repository.

Merchant workflow

Open Marketing > Search Performance to:

  1. Choose a store view and five eligible searches from recent search history.
  2. Compare the current search configuration with a proposal that increases product-name weighting, then rate the returned products. Save a review and return to it later.
  3. Inspect the comparison and regressions. Keep the current settings, or explicitly apply an eligible improvement and retain the option to restore the preceding state.

Applying or restoring requires a separate permission. An accepted comparison alone does not change storefront search. See Guided merchant reviews.

Advanced evaluation

Marketing > OpenSearch Relevance Workbench provides query snapshot preview and approval, native baseline capture, bounded field-boost candidates, human judgments, offline experiments, evidence export, activation, and rollback.

  • Every evaluation binds its query snapshot, configuration, judgments, and catalog-index evidence to immutable identities. Incomplete search responses and stale evidence are rejected.
  • NDCG@10, complete judged coverage, known-item checks, and an improvement threshold determine eligibility before explicit acceptance.
  • Field boosts change only existing supported query fields. Storefront activation applies to basic catalog search; GraphQL baseline evaluation is separate.
  • With OpenSearch Hybrid, evaluation targets its native lexical candidate stage. The module does not tune embeddings, fusion weights, generations, or pipelines, or measure the final Hybrid ranking.
  • Schedules prepare local drafts for review. They cannot approve snapshots, submit paid judgments, or activate search.
  • Evidence exports exclude query text and cannot be imported to execute a change. Remote cleanup is an ownership preview only.

Offline scores describe the reviewed sample. They do not establish revenue lift or ranking quality across the entire catalog.

Requirements

Component Requirement or qualification
Mage-OS 3.5.x; installed fixture uses 3.4.0
PHP Package accepts 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5; installed Mage-OS fixture uses 8.4
OpenSearch 3.8.0 with Search Relevance and ML Commons 3.8.0.0
OpenSearch Hybrid Optional, separate module
Docker Required for the integration and installed-system test fixtures

The Mage-OS 3.5.x target above is not yet reflected in Composer: the current package restricts Mage-OS dependencies to 3.4.*. Installed qualification remains on 3.4.0; this snapshot does not establish installation or compatibility on 3.5.x.

The human workflow uses the pinned standard OpenSearch image. LLM judgments require the dependency-corrected experimental runtime described in LLM operations. Other Magento distributions and OpenSearch versions have not been qualified.

Local checks

composer install
composer validate --strict --no-check-publish
composer test:unit
composer lint
composer analyse

See CI fixtures for OpenSearch, security, and installed Mage-OS checks. Synthetic fixture results establish technical behavior, not merchant acceptance.
